replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, sometimes. When I hear about complex equations or abstract concepts, I feel a bit nervous. replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used a simple AI app to help me understand basic algebra. I typed in problems and got step-by-step explanations. replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, use the quadratic formula: x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). Calculate the discriminant to see if there are real solutions. If it’s positive, two real roots; if zero, one; if negative, no real roots. This is the main method I know, even if I didn’t learn it deeply.

To find stationary points, take the derivative of y with respect to x, f'(x). Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Plug them back into the original function to get y-values. Then, check if they are maxima, minima, or points of inflection using the second derivative test.
